findings: Provenance: In silico postmortems must capture system state (OS/CPU/GPU architecture, driver versions), software dependencies (lockfiles, container SHAs), configuration lineage (compiler flags, random seeds, environment variables), and input data integrity (cryptographic SHA-256 hashes of all input files).

Hypothesis Falsifiability: To ensure hypotheses can be falsified, experiments must pre-register expectations, define boundary values, establish statistical thresholds, use explicit control baselines, and formally classify results as HELD, REFUTED, or INCONCLUSIVE based on pre-defined criteria.

Unexpected Anomaly Tracking: Tracking anomalies includes identifying physical/mathematical constraint violations (e.g., energy conservation drift in MD, exploding gradients or NaNs in ML), hardware-level errors (ECC memory issues, scheduler faults), and semantic anomalies (silent bugs, zero-variance outputs).

Decision Lineage: Documentation of decision lineage must include manual intervention logs, hyperparameter tuning paths, data exclusion rationale, Root Cause Analysis (RCA) diagnostic steps, and verdict overrides with explicit human justification.
query: Essential elements of a scientific postmortem for in silico experiments

title: Agentic Science NLM Research — Implications for bathos, maraxiom, and praxia evolution
query: Research on hypothesis integrity, nonrepudiation, AI scientist rigor, and adversarial science design
findings: Hypothesis Integrity Mechanisms (DR-1): Epistemic vigilance distinguishes between debate-as-refinement (post-hoc, no commitment) and cryptographic commitment (pre-execution, tamper-evident). Current practice in AI-assisted science lacks the latter, enabling constraint drop and implementation drift without detection.

Nonrepudiation Gap (DR-2): K-Veritas framework (arxiv 2605.08586) shows computational pre-registration is feasible; researchers can commit to execution plan before running, creating nonrepudiable records. Conferences increasingly expect this; maraxiom should integrate.

AI Scientist Failure Modes (DR-3): AI Scientist v1 exhibits 3.57× step amplification under termination poisoning, constraint drop (100% of agents tested), implementation drift (semantic divergence between declared and executed plan), and exception swallowing (errors silenced, outcomes corrupted).

Co-Scientist Commitment Artifacts (Q-1): Generate→debate→evolve does NOT commit hypotheses pre-execution. Minimum viable artifact = tamper-evident pre-registration file written BEFORE subprocess launch, separate from outcome schema.

Single-Run Validity (Q-2): POPPER falsification-first standard: one pre-registered pass is NOT verification; single run proves only that ONE execution met criteria, not that hypothesis is validated. Errored experiments should record outcome='error', not evaluate pass/fail conditions against partial results.

AI Scientist Drift Signals (Q-3): Constraint drop documented; implementation drift visible via semantic provenance graphs + explicit session rationales + complete code traces. Must distinguish revision (intentional, logged) from drift (unintended, discoverable only by diff inspection).

Adversarial Experiments Scope (Q-4): Adversarial = designed to falsify, but pre-registration alone does NOT test load-bearing capacity. Solo researcher must repurpose their own AI as adversary; requires defining 'what would break this?' before execution.

Rigor Signal Discriminability (Q-5): Outcome label entropy, unfired decision branches, residual branch rate, sidecar bypass rate, extra result fields empirically discriminate rigor from ad-hoc; thresholds from literature (~30% bypass rate = anomaly).

Gate Error Payload Structure (Q-6): Open-ended natural language instructions trigger agent verification regression (LoopTrap). MCP gate payloads must ground in raw data + structured taxonomy labels; error taxonomy prevents loops where agent revises error description infinitely.

bathos: Pre-execution Manifest Locking: Sidecar hash at bth run time is correct; also add optional `bth hypothesis lock` command that writes a pre-execution manifest file (timestamp + hypothesis + outcome_schema + git_sha + user + signatures) BEFORE subprocess launch. This makes the commitment artifact explicit, separate from the outcome schema, and nonrepudiable. Store manifest path in run record.

Error Outcome Handling: Implement outcome='error' as first-class outcome label. Errored experiments must NOT evaluate pass/fail/marginal conditions against partial results. Sidecar validator should reject conditions that reference fields absent in error cases. At run end, if subprocess exits nonzero or core dumps, force outcome='error' regardless of result_schema fields present.

Falsification-First Gate: Add `[falsification]` section to sidecar schema — required field 'breaks_when' that states the condition under which hypothesis would be REFUTED. This forces researchers to define discriminating conditions pre-execution. Validator checks that at least one outcome.fail condition is strict (e.g., numerical threshold, not vague). `bth sprint-audit` flags experiments lacking defined falsification.

Sprint Anomaly Signals: Formalize `bth sprint-audit` to flag rigor anomalies with thresholds from literature: outcome_label_entropy < 0.5 (suggests all runs pass/fail trivially), sidecar_bypass_rate > 0.3 (>30% of runs used --no-sidecar or --agent-mode), unfired_decision_branches > 0.4 (>40% of outcomes never selected), extra_result_fields_rate > 0.2 (fields in results not in schema). Generate risk report with counts and affected run IDs.

Agentic Integrity Gate Enhancement: When --agent-mode is set, enforce hypothesis lock BEFORE agent receives execution parameters. Sidecar hash + pre-execution manifest hash both recorded in run metadata. At run end, if sidecar_hash changes OR manifest_hash changes, outcome is marked 'REVISION' and flagged in sprint-audit. --derived-from can reference locked manifest of parent experiment.

Gate Error Taxonomy: MCP tools (postmortem_validate, gate checks) must return errors with structured payload: {error_code: str, taxonomy_label: str, raw_data: dict, resolution_hint: str}. Error codes: 'sidecar_parse_error', 'condition_eval_error', 'result_schema_mismatch', 'hypothesis_lock_missing', 'outcome_ambiguous'. Avoid natural language error messages that invite agent re-interpretation loops.
maraxiom: Nonrepudiation Integration: Maraxiom should accept and validate bathos pre-execution manifest files as nonrepudiation evidence. Manuscript claims should be traceable to (1) sidecar hypothesis hash, (2) pre-execution manifest, (3) run record, (4) result files. Provide `maraxiom cite-bathos-run` command to auto-generate provenance citations with reproducibility links.

Adversarial Peer Review Pipeline: Publishers shifting to adversarial review (reviewer deploys agent to break claims). Maraxiom should support runnable analysis packages alongside manuscripts: tar.zst with sidecar TOMLs + scripts + lockfiles + sample data. Reviewer can `bth run` each experiment locally and attempt adversarial variations. Document the 'what would break this?' framework as the standard for adversarial design.

Provenance Graph Auto-Generation: W3C PROV standard links claims → evidence → code execution. Maraxiom could auto-generate PROV graphs from bathos lineage data (`bth lineage --format prov`). Manuscript figures cite specific run IDs; readers can fetch run lineage and verify claim-to-evidence chain. Adds verifiability layer without requiring external tooling.

Falsification-First Publishing: Require manuscripts to pre-register primary hypotheses + expected falsification conditions BEFORE results are disclosed. Maraxiom companion sidecar (separate from code sidecars) states the paper's main claims as outcome conditions. Reviewers check: (a) conditions are falsifiable (not tautological), (b) at least one outcome is failure/refutation, (c) results align with pre-registered classifications.
praxia: Structured Gate Error Taxonomy: Praxia's MCP gate errors (in tools like postmortem_validate, sprint_audit) must use structured taxonomy instead of natural language. Define error_code enum: 'hypothesis_lock_missing', 'sidecar_hash_mismatch', 'outcome_evaluation_error', 'result_schema_violation', 'anomaly_flag_triggered'. Each error returns {error_code, taxonomy_label, raw_data_sample, resolution_hint}. This prevents agents from triggering verification regression loops where error description is revised infinitely.

Transduction Hook Coverage: NLM integration (`nlm.jsonl`) currently covers note_create/note_list. Add hooks for async notebook operations: notebook_query_start, notebook_query_end, notebook_query_status, artifact_create_start, artifact_create_end. Post-tool-use handlers log these events to transduction log with notebook_id and query hash for full traceability.

Sprint Composer Pre-Registration Gate: When dispatching science agents (experiment execution, validation, analysis), sprint-composer should enforce hypothesis commitment as a GATE, not a suggestion. Before experiment node runs, pre-registration artifact must exist and be locked. If agent creates/modifies sidecar mid-sprint, that is a REVISION (tracked separately), not an update. Use `--derived-from` to link revision to parent and document rationale.

Loop Step Budget Enforcement: LoopTrap research shows 3.57× average step amplification when agents encounter open-ended verification gates. Orchestrator should track loop step depth and enforce a per-task budget (default: 20 steps for science tasks, 50 for complex orchestration). If budget exhausted, surface blocker with evidence (step log + decision tree) rather than escalating to agent recursively.

Agentic Rigor Audit Trail: When agents use --agent-mode or --no-sidecar, record: (1) agent_id, (2) session_id, (3) decision rationale (why was this run conducted?), (4) constraint_check_results (were all declared constraints satisfied?), (5) semantic_provenance_hash (did execution match declared plan?). Postmortem should cross-check these fields against run outcomes. If decision_rationale missing or semantics diverged, flag as potential drift.
